predict.q: Who do you think built the first working pendulum clock?
predict.reveal: Christiaan Huygens built the first working pendulum clock in 1656. Galileo had designed one years earlier, but never finished building it.

explain.text:
Before the pendulum, the best clocks drifted by about a quarter of an hour a day. A pendulum swings at a steady beat, so a clock that counts its swings keeps far better time.

Galileo noticed the steady beat around 1602 and, late in life, sketched a clock that would use it. Christiaan Huygens built the first working pendulum clock in 1656, and it drifted by less than a minute a day. Who deserves the credit is still argued over.

say.prompt: In your own words: why did the pendulum make clocks so much more accurate?
rubric: A pendulum swings at a steady, regular beat
The clock counts swings to keep time
say.model: A pendulum swings at a steady beat that hardly changes, so a clock that counts those swings keeps much more regular time than one driven by a spring or a falling weight alone.

views.label: Credit Galileo
views.text: He discovered the steady beat and designed the first pendulum clock. Huygens built on his idea.

views.label: Credit Huygens
views.text: An idea on paper is not a clock. Huygens solved the hard parts and built one that worked.
